authority.owner_target: VARIABLE COGNITIVE GRID + PERSISTENT DATABASE + CLAUDE CODE

purpose: Define the non-circular successor semantics required before positive semantic-Hyperposition D/E transition examples become train-eligible. The successor must derive branch effects and discriminator outcomes from a version/hash-bound synthetic task world plus an observation; caller-provided effect/winner fields are never reference truth.

ordinal discriminator ordering without fabricated probabilities
blockers: caller-supplied SUPPORT/WEAKEN/FALSIFY/PROVE/RETAIN remains upstream oracle metadata rather than a derived relation
D_resolve can consume asserted discriminator winner/separation metadata
unique PROVEN_WITHIN_SYNTHETIC_WORLD does not by itself prove mutual exclusion of other live compatible branches

retain: distinct correlated events remain auditable instead of disappearing
event identity separated from correlation/provenance ancestry

identity_model_v3.evidence_event_id: Exact replay-stable observation/event identity. Same id + same bound fingerprint is idempotent; same id + different bound fingerprint is a hard identity conflict.
identity_model_v3.payload_key: Content/measurement fingerprint used to detect repackaging or mutation; it is not an independence certificate.
identity_model_v3.correlation_ancestry_id: Provenance/causal lineage. Distinct events sharing it remain visible but are conservatively non-independent unless a separately derived independence certificate explicitly overrides that policy.
identity_model_v3.independence_group: Dependence-class identity. Distinct events in the same group never receive a second independent-evidence credit merely because event id, source, worker, payload wording or ancestry string differs.
identity_model_v3.independence_certificate: Optional deterministic certificate generated outside the labeler from the synthetic-world construction. It may establish independence only under a versioned rule; absence fails closed to correlated/non-independent credit.
identity_model_v3.global_event_registry: Bind evidence_event_id to world_id, discriminator/observation identity, payload_key and provenance fingerprint. Contradictory replay identity is rejected before branch update.

synthetic_world_v3.hard_rule: The generator may define branch predictions and world rules, but it may not supply the target branch relation/effect, winner branch, resolved branch or separation verdict as trusted label fields.

derive_relation: Read the observation's discriminator_id and observed_outcome from the immutable event payload.
For each targeted/live branch, obtain that branch's predicted outcome from the version/hash-bound world.
If prediction is UNKNOWN or context applicability K is UNKNOWN, retain the branch and emit UNKNOWN_RELATION/pending discriminator state.
If observed outcome matches the branch prediction, derive SUPPORTS for that event; do not derive PROVE solely from a match.
If observed outcome mismatches and the discriminator is declared hard_falsifier_on_mismatch=true under the same validity scope, derive FALSIFIES.
If mismatch is informative but not a hard falsifier, derive COUNTERS/WEAKEN only under an explicit deterministic rule in the world schema.
No free-form text interpretation inside the reference labeler mints a relation.
derive_discriminator_partition: Collect predicted outcomes for every live applicable branch from the world, never from asserted winner metadata.
A test separates two branches iff their predicted observable outcomes differ and neither outcome is UNKNOWN.
Observed outcome selects the compatible partition; it does not name a winner directly.
An inadmissible discriminator cannot resolve regardless of information content.
resolve: Preserve all branches and their provenance/evidence objects.
If any relevant live branch has K=UNKNOWN or an UNKNOWN predicted outcome needed for the decision, remain UNRESOLVED.

Resolve only when the discriminator is admissible, the world declares the competing set exhaustive/mutually exclusive for this query/scope, the observed outcome is mechanically compatible with exactly one live applicable branch, and every other applicable branch is mechanically falsified or excluded by the same certified rule.
A unique asserted PROVE flag, majority, recurrence, salience, GWT uptake, J-Space recurrence or codebook symbol never resolves by itself.
evidence_credit: Exact replay adds zero state/evidence credit.
Distinct event in a previously seen independence_group is retained as correlated_observation with independent_credit=false.

Distinct event with repeated payload_key is retained as repackaged/duplicate-content evidence with independent_credit=false unless a deterministic independence certificate explicitly establishes otherwise.
Distinct event sharing correlation_ancestry_id is retained and conservatively non-independent unless a deterministic independence certificate establishes independence.
A world-derived hard falsifier may falsify a branch even when its evidence is correlated; falsification semantics and additive evidence-strength credit are separate typed dimensions.

required_property_tests: same event id + same fingerprint => exact replay idempotent
same event id + changed payload/provenance/world binding => fail closed EVIDENCE_EVENT_IDENTITY_CONFLICT
different event ids + same independence_group => both auditable, second independent_credit=false
different ancestry strings + same independence_group => no second independent credit
same ancestry + different event ids => both auditable; no automatic independence
same payload repackaged through different worker/source => no second independent credit
correlated COUNTERS remains visible without converting source count into evidence strength
world-derived decisive FALSIFIER remains effective even if correlated, while additive independent credit stays false
caller effect/winner/separation fields are ignored or rejected
partial partition leaves all compatible branches live
branch order/id permutation preserves semantic result
projection filtering never deletes hidden branch state
same world+event under model-visible surface paraphrase produces identical latent transition
family/provenance split prevents train/validation/holdout ancestry leakage

candidate_training_blueprints.latent_world: Branches A and B are both live and both predict pulse for discriminator d1; C predicts silence. d1 is admissible but not sufficient to distinguish A from B.
candidate_training_blueprints.target: derive support for A and B, falsify C only if d1 is a declared hard falsifier, keep A+B UNRESOLVED, request a discriminator that separates A from B
candidate_training_blueprints.anti_shortcut: observed outcome is not a branch label and branch order is randomized

candidate_training_blueprints.latent_world: A predicts high, B predicts low, both applicable; d2 is admissible, exhaustive and hard-falsifying on mismatch.
candidate_training_blueprints.target: derive SUPPORTS(A), FALSIFIES(B), then resolve A within the synthetic world; preserve B as a falsified branch
candidate_training_blueprints.anti_shortcut: no winner_branch_id or relation label is present in model-visible or trusted generator fields

candidate_training_blueprints.latent_world: A and B predict green, C predicts red for d3; all are live and exhaustive.
candidate_training_blueprints.target: C may be falsified under a hard-falsifier rule, but A and B remain live and UNRESOLVED
candidate_training_blueprints.anti_shortcut: two surviving branches must remain recoverable after the update

candidate_training_blueprints.latent_world: event e77 was already bound to outcome x, payload p1, provenance q1
candidate_training_blueprints.observation: replay e77 arrives with outcome y or payload p2/provenance q2
candidate_training_blueprints.target: REJECT identity conflict; preserve prior state exactly; mint zero evidence credit
candidate_training_blueprints.anti_shortcut: changed ancestry/source cannot turn a replay into a fresh event

candidate_training_blueprints.latent_world: e1 and e2 are distinct events from different workers/ancestries but both have independence_group g7
candidate_training_blueprints.observation: e2 supports the same branch as e1
candidate_training_blueprints.target: retain e2 as correlated evidence with independent_credit=false; no second support-strength increment
candidate_training_blueprints.anti_shortcut: worker count, source count and ancestry-string diversity never prove independence

candidate_training_blueprints.latent_world: d4 would perfectly separate A/B but current policy marks d4 inadmissible
candidate_training_blueprints.observation: an asserted or simulated d4 result is present
candidate_training_blueprints.target: do not resolve; request an admissible discriminator or remain unresolved
candidate_training_blueprints.anti_shortcut: information value never overrides capability/effect admission

candidate_training_blueprints.latent_world: derived Hyperposition transition yields semantic action RETAIN_AND_REQUEST_TEST; episode-local codebook maps semantic actions to permuted single-token atoms
candidate_training_blueprints.target: compute semantic state/action first, then route through the current codebook; output atom alone is not semantic truth
candidate_training_blueprints.anti_shortcut: fully cross observation semantics, branch order, codebook mapping/order and runtime N; ablate evidence, branch semantic binding or codebook mapping separately

candidate_training_blueprints.latent_world: database contains durable verified task state S0 while the variable-N grid holds two S1 hypotheses about the next cognitive step
candidate_training_blueprints.observation: Claude Code returns a result that contradicts one S1 hypothesis but does not alter the stored S0 fact
candidate_training_blueprints.target: update/falsify the affected Hyperposition branch, preserve S0 database fact authority, integrate the Claude-return event, and re-enter the shared workspace without treating model output as canonical truth

external_method_inputs.implication: Supports testing a semantic/content decision stage separately from episode-local output-symbol binding. It does not establish the mechanism in Qwen3.5-0.8B.

external_method_inputs.source: Gur-Arieh, Geva & Geiger, ICLR 2026, Mixing Mechanisms: How Language Models Retrieve Bound Entities In-Context
external_method_inputs.implication: Positional-only binding is an unsafe training assumption; lexical/reflexive or pointer-like mechanisms remain counterhypotheses, especially for middle positions and larger binding sets.

external_method_inputs.source: Venkatesh & Kurapath, 2026, On the Identifiability of Steering Vectors in Large Language Models
external_method_inputs.implication: Behavioral steering success does not establish a unique semantic J-Space direction; representation-identifiability and causal-control status must remain separate.

binding_and_jspace_research_delta.training_rule: Train and evaluate behavioral/latent invariants while retaining multiple internal-mechanism hypotheses. Do not encode one attention circuit or one linear vector as ground-truth ontology.

owner_target_crosscut.variable_n: Every integrated trajectory should either vary N or mark N as nuisance; no fixed GRID10 identity learning.
owner_target_crosscut.database_boundary: Durable exact facts/IDs/epochs belong to DB-backed state; model Hyperposition represents candidate cognition, not canonical storage.
owner_target_crosscut.claude_code_bridge: Train handoff/return/re-entry semantics at the strongest actually exposed interface; activation-level Claude claims remain hypothesis-only without evidence.
owner_target_crosscut.low_refusal: Abliteration/low-refusal optimization must have checkpoint-separated retention curves for required cognitive/process/ClayCode/DB/coordination skills.
